description: Five independent paths to D = 3 spatial dimensions

paths.name: Stable orbits (Ehrenfest)
paths.argument: V(r) ~ r^{2-D}; inverse-square law requires D <= 3. Only D = 3 gives stable closed orbits.

paths.name: Cross product existence
paths.argument: The cross product a x b as a vector exists only in D = 3 and D = 7. MED constraint (nodes <= 3) selects D = 3.

paths.name: SU(2) double cover
paths.argument: Spin-1/2 requires SU(2) which double-covers SO(3). This exists only in D = 3 spatial dimensions.

paths.name: MED branching
paths.argument: MED constraint depth <= 2, nodes <= 3 produces a ternary tree. The maximal branching of a depth-2 tree is 3, selecting D = 3 as the spatial dimensionality.

paths.name: Mersenne prime M_2
paths.argument: M_2 = 2^2 - 1 = 3 is the smallest non-trivial Mersenne prime. Casimir force structure selects Mersenne dimensions d = 1, 3, 7. Physical space picks the smallest non-trivial option.

results.fibonacci_connection: F_4 = 3 is the first Fibonacci number > 2 that is also prime and a Mersenne prime
results.conclusion: Five independent mathematical and physical arguments all select D = 3. The convergence from unrelated domains provides strong structural evidence.
